title: The night watchman's round

data.source: Poincare (1890), Kac (1947). Computed on the worked rotor of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md section IV and on a golden-mean rotation, seeded.

prediction: The mean time between cuts on the worked rotor is Kac's return time to the thin cut set, 181.38 steps or 1.8138 time units; Kac does not give the two unequal half-turns; and reading Omega as the measure of the coherent region, as the wider notes do, gives a return time near 1 step instead.
baseline: Kac's lemma (1947): mean return time to a set equals one over its measure. Poincare's recurrence theorem (1890).
why: The cut rate is Kac's lemma applied to the cut set, to the decimal places shown, and says nothing more than the lemma; the lemma gives the mean only, not the 1.2092 and 2.4184 of the two halves. The wider notes' claim M19 (their tier T1, conjecture) names the wrong set: return to the coherent region takes about one step, a factor of 180 off here and a different factor at a different step size. Recurrence is not guaranteed for CRR's own rotor: pushed weakly it stalls, which R2 (ASSUMPTION) already allows.
